text: What is the time complexity of the 'heapify' operation for an array of N elements?
explanation: Building a heap from an unordered array using the bottom-up heapify approach takes O(n) time.

text: In a Max-Heap, where is the largest element located?
explanation: The fundamental property of a max-heap is that the parent is always greater than or equal to its children.

text: Which C++ STL container implements a Priority Queue?
explanation: std::priority_queue provides the functionality of a max-heap by default in C++.

text: What is the complexity of deleting the root (pop) in a Binary Heap?
explanation: Popping requires swapping the root with the last leaf and 'bubbling down', taking logarithmic time.

text: If a heap is stored in an array starting at index 1, where are the children of node at index 'i'?
explanation: The standard array representation of a binary tree uses 2i and 2i+1 for left and right children.

text: Which Java class is used to implement a Min-Heap or Max-Heap?
explanation: java.util.PriorityQueue is the standard heap implementation in Java (Min-Heap by default).

text: How do you create a Max-Heap using PriorityQueue in Java?
explanation: Passing a reverse order comparator converts the default Min-Heap into a Max-Heap.

text: What is the complexity of peek() on a Java PriorityQueue?
explanation: Peek simply returns the element at the top (index 0), which is constant time.

text: In a Heap, which property must every node satisfy compared to its children?
options: The Heap property (either always >= or always <=)
correctAnswer: The Heap property (either always >= or always <=)
explanation: A heap is defined by its consistent relationship between parents and children.

text: Complexity of adding an element (offer) to a Java PriorityQueue?
explanation: Adding requires 'bubbling up' to restore the heap property, which takes O(log n).

text: Which module in Python contains the heap implementation?
explanation: The 'heapq' module provides functions to maintain a list as a min-heap.

text: What kind of heap does Python's 'heapq' module implement by default?
explanation: heapq functions (heappush, heappop) maintain min-heap properties.

text: How do you convert an existing list 'li' into a heap in-place in Python?
explanation: heapify() reorganizes the list elements to satisfy heap properties in O(n) time.

text: What is the time complexity of 'heapq.heappush()' in Python?
explanation: Inserting an element into a heap requires a logarithmic number of comparisons and swaps.

text: To implement a Max-Heap in Python using 'heapq', what common trick is used?
explanation: Negating the numbers makes the smallest value (most negative) the 'highest', effectively simulating a max-heap.

text: Is there a built-in Heap or Priority Queue class in standard JavaScript?
explanation: Standard JS (ES6) does not include a Priority Queue; developers must use a library or implement it.

text: How would you implement a Min-Heap 'push' using a JS array?
explanation: Adding to the end and swapping with the parent until properties are met is the standard heap insertion.

text: Complexity of building a heap from an array by sorting it in JS?
explanation: Sorting an array takes O(n log n), which is slower than the O(n) heapify algorithm.

text: In a Complete Binary Tree (Heap), what is the index of the parent of node at index 'i' (0-indexed)?
explanation: The inverse of child indexing (2i+1, 2i+2) is (i-1)/2.

text: Which operation is O(1) in a Heap?
explanation: Accessing the root element is always constant time.

text: Which Graph traversal uses a Queue?
explanation: BFS uses a FIFO queue to visit nodes level-by-level.

text: In an Adjacency Matrix for a graph with V vertices, what is the space complexity?
explanation: An adjacency matrix stores a V x V grid of connections.

text: Which representation is better for a Sparse Graph (few edges)?
explanation: Adjacency lists only store existing edges, saving space when E << V^2.

text: What is the time complexity of BFS or DFS on a graph with V vertices and E edges?
explanation: Both algorithms visit every vertex and every edge once.

text: In a directed graph, if there is an edge from A to B, does that mean there is an edge from B to A?
options: Only if it is a tree
explanation: Directed edges (arrows) have a specific destination and are one-way unless a reverse edge exists.

text: Which Graph algorithm uses a Stack (or Recursion)?
explanation: Depth-First Search explores as deep as possible before backtracking, naturally matching LIFO/Stack behavior.

text: In an undirected graph, what is the relation between the Adjacency Matrix values [i][j] and [j][i]?
explanation: Undirected graphs are symmetric; an edge from i to j is also an edge from j to i.

text: How do you avoid visiting the same node twice in a Graph traversal?
explanation: Tracking visited nodes prevents infinite loops in graphs with cycles.

text: What defines a 'Connected Graph'?
options: There is a path between every pair of vertices
correctAnswer: There is a path between every pair of vertices
explanation: A graph is connected if you can reach any vertex from any other vertex.

text: What is the complexity of checking if an edge exists between 'u' and 'v' in an Adjacency Matrix?
explanation: Matrices provide direct access to the connection status at matrix[u][v].

text: Which Python structure is most commonly used for an Adjacency List?
explanation: Dictionaries allow O(1) lookup of a node's entire neighbor list.

text: In a directed acyclic graph (DAG), what special sorting can be performed?
explanation: Topological sort orders nodes such that for every edge u->v, u comes before v.

text: What does a Cycle in a graph represent?
options: A path that starts and ends at the same vertex
correctAnswer: A path that starts and ends at the same vertex
explanation: A cycle is a closed path where the first and last vertices are identical.

text: Complexity of DFS on a graph using an Adjacency Matrix?
explanation: When using a matrix, you must scan all V possible connections for every vertex visit.

text: Which algorithm finds the Shortest Path in an unweighted graph?
explanation: BFS explores nodes level by level, ensuring the first time a target is reached, it is via the shortest path.

text: How do you represent a Graph in JavaScript natively?
options: Using a class with an object/map
Graphs are not possible in JS
explanation: JS objects/Maps or nested arrays are flexible enough to represent edges and vertices.

text: In a DFS implementation, which helper data structure is typically used to manage the nodes for backtracking?
explanation: DFS follows a path deep before returning, which matches the LIFO (Last-In-First-Out) behavior of a stack.

text: What is the degree of a vertex in an undirected graph?
options: Number of edges connected to it
The total edges in the graph
Number of cycles it belongs to
correctAnswer: Number of edges connected to it
explanation: Degree counts how many edges touch the vertex.

text: In a Weighted Graph, what extra info is stored with each edge?
explanation: Weights represent the cost or distance for traversing that specific edge.

text: Which graph traversal is more 'memory efficient' for a very wide tree?
explanation: DFS only stores nodes on the current path, whereas BFS must store all nodes at the current level (which can be huge in a wide tree).
